page.layout: One page of text. At the head, the page number "(31)" and the plate number "I.". Below them, two woodcut coins one above the other, each with a Hebrew legend around its rim. Under the coins, a centred caption in larger type, two lines. At the foot left, the signature "E 4"; at the foot right, the plate number "II.". No running head, no margin notes.

main_text.l: Siclus Argenteus, in Musæo Nicolai Crassi J.C. Veneti.

page.notes: The page carries two woodcut illustrations of silver shekels (siclus argenteus), reproduced as figures and not transcribed as text. The upper coin shows a chalice on a stand, with letters around the rim. The lower coin shows a branched plant (a stem with three buds or flowers), with letters around the rim. The rim legends are in Hebrew (paleo-Hebrew letterforms) and are too small and worn to read reliably, so both are marked illegible; the letter counts are estimates. The caption "Crassi" is printed with a long s that looks like a double f; it is transcribed with a plain s. "Musæo" is printed "Mufæo" with a long s, also transcribed with a plain s. "I." and "II." are plate or figure numbers, so they are set as paragraphs, not headings. The page number "(31)" is printed at the head.
